readings: You have the words of eternal life
2027-03-03.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). Mid-Fast: the Great Fast reaches its midpoint today. In some parishes the Cross is honoured with special prayers; follow local custom.
2027-03-03.verse: Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.
theo: Today the Great Fast reaches its midpoint. The calendar marks this Wednesday as Mid-Fast: as many days lie behind us as before us, and the Resurrection is now nearer than Ash Monday. It is a good day to stop, look back honestly, and begin again. The first reading shows a quarrel that every Kerala family knows. Abram and his nephew Lot have grown rich, “and there was strife between the herders of Abram's livestock and the herders of Lot's livestock.” Abram is the elder; by custom he could choose first. Instead he says: “Let there be no strife between you and me, and between your herders and my herders; for we are kindred. Is not the whole land before you?” Lot looks with his eyes and chooses the best: the plain of the Jordan, “well watered everywhere like the garden of the LORD”, and he moves his tent “as far as Sodom.” Then, when Abram has let go, God speaks: “Raise your eyes now, and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward; for all the land that you see I will give to you and to your offspring forever.” The man who gave up the first choice receives everything. Many of our families carry wounds from partitions of land and houses, brothers who have not spoken for years over a boundary stone. Mid-Fast is a good day to say Abram's sentence: we are kindred.

The second reading tells of the fall of Ai. God says to Joshua: “Stretch out the sword that is in your hand toward Ai; for I will give it into your hand.” Joshua does not lower his hand until the battle is over, and the king of Ai is hanged on a tree until evening and taken down at sunset. It is a fierce story from a fierce age. Origen, preaching on this chapter, read it in the light of the Cross (in substance): the outstretched hand of Joshua, whose name is the same as the name of Jesus, points to the arms of Christ stretched out on the wood, and the enemy hanged on the tree points to the powers of evil that Christ disarmed on the Cross, “triumphing over them in it” (Colossians 2:15). At the middle of the fast the Church holds up the Cross before us: the battle is not ours alone, and it has already been won.

Paul longs for the salvation of his people, who have “a zeal for God”, and he shows how near salvation is: “The word is near you, on your lips and in your heart”; “if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.” And it is for all: “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.” The Gospel takes us to the end of the great sermon on the Bread of Life. Jesus has said that his flesh is true food and his blood true drink, and many disciples say: “This teaching is difficult; who can accept it?” They do not misunderstand him; they understand him and leave. “Because of this many of his disciples turned back and no longer went about with him.” Jesus does not soften his words or call them back with a gentler explanation. He turns to the Twelve: “Do you also wish to go away?” Peter answers for the Church of every age: “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life. We have come to believe and know that you are the Holy One of God.” At the midpoint of the fast, some of us are tired, and some have quietly given up. Jesus asks the same question. Peter's answer is still the only one that makes sense.

The hard teaching of the Bread of Life, and Peter's answer.

live: If there is a quarrel over property or inheritance in your family, take one step toward peace before Palm Sunday.
Look back over the first half of the fast; take up again one resolution you have dropped, and add a visit to the Blessed Sacrament this week.
2027-03-03.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, at the middle of the fast you ask us whether we too wish to go away. We answer with Peter: to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life. Give us the generosity of Abram to let go for the sake of peace, the faith to confess you with our lips and believe in our hearts, and the strength to walk the rest of the way to your Cross and Resurrection. Amen.
altar: The teaching that made many disciples leave is the gift we receive at every Holy Qurbana: the flesh of the Son of Man given for the life of the world. We stay, because he has the words of eternal life.

quick: Mid-Fast: the fast reaches its midpoint; look back and begin again.

2027-03-03.question: Halfway through the fast, am I still walking with Jesus, or have I quietly turned back?

family.explain: Jesus told the people that he would give them his own body and blood as food. Many found this too hard and went away. Jesus asked his twelve apostles: do you want to go away too? Peter said: Lord, where would we go? Only you have the words that give eternal life. Jesus gives us this food at every Holy Qurbana.
family.intention: We pray for all who have given up their Lenten promises, that they may begin again.
family.ask: Ask: “Which of our Lenten promises have we forgotten? Let us start again today.”

illus: Two brothers near Pala had not spoken for twelve years because of a boundary between their rubber plots, a strip of land only four metres wide. On Mid-Fast Wednesday the elder brother heard the reading about Abram and Lot. That evening he walked to his brother's house with the property papers and said: “Take the strip. We are brothers.” His brother cried. The next Sunday the two families sat together at the Holy Qurbana for the first time in twelve years.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, at the middle of the fast we come to you. To whom else can we go? Amen.
share: Let there be no strife between you and me; for we are kindred (Genesis 13:8). With whom am I not at peace?
Stretch out the sword that is in your hand (Joshua 8:18). Do I fight my battles alone, or under the Cross?
Do you also wish to go away? (John 6:67). Where am I tempted to turn back?
pm.resp: Lord, you have the words of eternal life.
interc: For the Church, that she may hold up the Cross before the world.
For families divided by quarrels over property, that they may be reconciled.
For those who have given up the fast, that they may begin again.
For those who find the teaching of the Holy Qurbana hard, that they may come to believe.
For our group, that we may stay with Jesus to the end.
pm.close: Father, at the middle of this fast we thank you for the days that are past and entrust to you the days that remain. Keep us with your Son, who has the words of eternal life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today is Mid-Fast, the middle of the Great Fast. It is a good day to look back honestly and to begin again.

Abram and Lot quarrel over land. Abram, the elder, says: let there be no strife between you and me, for we are kindred (Genesis 13:8), and he lets Lot choose first. Then God gives Abram all the land he can see. Many families carry the wound of a quarrel over property. Today, let us take one step toward peace.

Joshua stretches out his hand toward Ai and does not lower it until the battle is won. The Fathers saw in this outstretched hand a picture of Christ's arms stretched out on the Cross. At the middle of the fast, the Church holds up the Cross: our battle has already been won by him.

When Jesus says his flesh is true food, many disciples leave him. He asks the Twelve: do you also wish to go away? Peter answers: Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life (John 6:68). If we are tired today, let us make Peter's answer our own, and walk on to Easter. Amen.
kids: Children, when some people left Jesus, he asked his friends: will you leave me too? Peter said: Lord, where would we go? We want to stay with you! Let us tell Jesus today: I want to stay with you too.

sub: Peter's answer for the whole Church.

concl: At the middle of the fast, the Cross is held up and the question is asked again: do you also wish to go away?
Let go for the sake of peace, confess Jesus as Lord, and stay with the one who has the words of eternal life.
